q: Austrian must weight is measured in °KMW. What does one degree represent, and what is the minimum for Qualitätswein?
accept: klosterneuburger mostwaage grams of sugar per 100 grams of must, 15 kmw minimum
sugar as a weight percentage of the must, qualitatswein needs 15 kmw
grams of sugar per 100g of must and 15 kmw for qualitatswein
klosterneuburger mostwaage sugar by weight, minimum 15 kmw
ans: °Klosterneuburger Mostwaage = grams of sugar per 100 g of must (a weight percentage); Qualitätswein requires a minimum of 15° KMW
exp: KMW measures sugar by weight; the official conversion is °Oechsle = (°KMW × 4.54) + 0.022 × °KMW², so 15° KMW is 73° Oechsle and the two scales run at roughly five to one. Austria's whole ripeness ladder is written in KMW — Spätlese 19°, Auslese 21°, Beerenauslese and Eiswein 25°, Ausbruch 27°, TBA 30° — so a candidate quoting Oechsle figures is quoting German law. Note too that Austrian Kabinett (17° KMW, unchaptalized) is a Qualitätswein category, not a Prädikat.

q: Which region south of Vienna builds its whites on Zierfandler and Rotgipfler, and what is the traditional blend of the two called?
accept: thermenregion south of vienna, the blend is spatrot-rotgipfler
gumpoldskirchen in the thermenregion, spatrot rotgipfler
ans: The Thermenregion, centred on Gumpoldskirchen — the pair is co-blended as Spätrot-Rotgipfler (Zierfandler is locally called Spätrot)
exp: Zierfandler and Rotgipfler are siblings — both natural Traminer × Roter Veltliner offspring — and virtually the entire world planting of each sits in this one region, which is why they never appear in a blind-tasting grid but always in an oral. Zierfandler brings acid and spice, Rotgipfler weight and stone fruit. Zierfandler has no connection whatever to Zinfandel; the Thermenregion also grows serious Pinot Noir and St. Laurent around Tattendorf.

q: DNA analysis has settled Grüner Veltliner's parentage. What is it?
opts: Silvaner × Roter Veltliner, the grapes in its name
Traminer × Sankt Georgener-Rebe, a lone old vine
Riesling × Silvaner, an early Klosterneuburg crossing
exp: The second parent was found in 2000 as a single ancient vine at St. Georgen am Leithagebirge in Burgenland, and the cross was confirmed shortly after — Traminer's fingerprints explain Grüner's spice. The trap is the name: Austria's 'Veltliner' grapes (Roter, Frühroter, Brauner, Grüner) are a family only on the label, and Grüner is not a Silvaner relative despite a century of textbooks saying so.
